title: Test organization
summary: Unit tests next to the code (including private functions), integration tests in the tests directory, shared helpers, binary crates, and documentation tests.

sections: TRPL 11.3 Integration Tests for Binary Crates
CR Day 4 Other Types of Tests

blocks.md:
The Rust community thinks of tests in two groups:

- **Unit tests** are small and focused. Each tests one module in isolation, sits in the same file as the code, and may test **private** details.
- **Integration tests** are external. They use your library exactly as another crate would, only through its public API, and often exercise several modules together.

A third kind, **doc tests**, checks that the examples in your documentation still work.

blocks.title: Unit tests can reach private items
blocks.md: Because the `tests` module is a child of the module it tests, Rust's privacy rules let it use everything in its parent, private or not (chapter 7: children can see their ancestors' items). Whether to test private functions is a matter of taste; Rust allows it.

blocks.title: Integration tests
blocks.md: Integration tests live in a **`tests` directory** next to `src`. Cargo compiles **each file** in it as a separate crate, which imports your library by name:

blocks.code:
adder
├── Cargo.lock
├── Cargo.toml
├── src
│   └── lib.rs
└── tests
    ├── common
    │   └── mod.rs        (shared helpers, not a test file)
    └── integration_test.rs

blocks.explain: No `#[cfg(test)]` is needed: Cargo only compiles the `tests` directory for `cargo test`. Only `pub` items of `adder` are reachable, just as for any user of your crate.

blocks.code:
$ cargo test
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/deps/adder-1082c4b063a8fbe6)
running 1 test
test tests::internal ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ...

     Running tests/integration_test.rs (target/debug/deps/integration_test-1082c4b063a8fbe6)
running 1 test
test it_adds_two ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ...

   Doc-tests adder
running 0 tests
blocks.explain: Three sections: unit tests, then one section per integration test file, then doc tests. If a unit test fails, Cargo stops before running the integration tests.

blocks.title: Why tests/common/mod.rs and not tests/common.rs
blocks.md: Every `.rs` file directly in `tests/` is a test crate and appears in the report, even if it has no tests. Putting shared code in `tests/common/mod.rs` (a subdirectory) tells Cargo it is a module, not a test crate. Each test file then declares `mod common;`.

blocks.title: Binary crates
blocks.md: Integration tests can only `use` a **library** crate. A project with only `src/main.rs` cannot be integration-tested this way. That is one reason Rust projects keep `main.rs` small and put the logic in `src/lib.rs`: then `main` just calls into the library, and the library is fully testable. Chapter 12's project does exactly this.

blocks.title: Documentation tests
blocks.md: Documentation comments start with `///` and support Markdown. Code blocks in them are **compiled and run by `cargo test`** as doc tests. Examples in documentation therefore cannot silently go stale: if the API changes, the example fails.

blocks.explain: Common sections are `# Examples`, `# Panics`, `# Errors` (what errors a `Result` function returns and why) and `# Safety` (for `unsafe` functions). `cargo doc --open` turns these comments into HTML documentation (chapter 14).

blocks.title: A tested word-wrap
blocks.goal: Implement a public function on top of private helpers, where unit tests check both the helpers and the public behavior.
blocks.behavior:
`pub fn wrap(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String>` splits text into lines of at most `width` characters, breaking only at spaces. A single word longer than `width` goes on its own line unbroken. Runs of whitespace collapse to single spaces. Empty text gives an empty vector.

The tests also call two **private** helpers you must write (they test your building blocks):
- `fn words(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>`: the whitespace-separated words.
- `fn fits(line: &str, word: &str, width: usize) -> bool`: whether `word` can be added to `line` (with one space if `line` is not empty) without exceeding `width`. Count characters, not bytes.
hints: `fits`: if `line` is empty, `word.chars().count() <= width`; otherwise `line.chars().count() + 1 + word.chars().count() <= width`.

In `wrap`: keep a `current: String`; for each word, if it fits, push a space (when needed) and the word; otherwise push `current` into the result (if not empty) and start a new line with the word. Push the last line at the end.
blocks.solution_explain: The tests module is a child of the crate root, so it can call the private `words` and `fits`. Testing small helpers separately makes a failure in `wrap` easier to locate. An integration test in `tests/` could only call `wrap`.

questions.q: Can an integration test in `tests/api.rs` call a private function of your library?
options: No, it uses the crate like any external user: only `pub` items
questions.explanation: Each file in tests/ is a separate crate.

questions.q: Why put shared helpers in `tests/common/mod.rs` rather than `tests/common.rs`?
options: Files directly in tests/ are compiled as test crates and show up in the output
questions.explanation: A subdirectory module is not treated as a test crate.

questions.q: A project has only `src/main.rs`. What is the usual way to make its logic integration-testable?
options: Move the logic to `src/lib.rs` and keep main small
Integration tests are impossible in Rust
questions.explanation: Integration tests can only use a library crate.

questions.q: Code examples in `///` comments are compiled and run by `cargo test`.
Put the sections of `cargo test` output in the order they run.

points: Unit tests sit next to the code in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` and may test private items.
Integration tests live in `tests/`; each file is its own crate using only the public API.
Keep `main.rs` thin and logic in `lib.rs` so it can be integration-tested.
Examples in `///` doc comments run as doc tests, so documentation stays correct.

terms.def: A small test next to the code it tests, able to reach private items.
A test in the tests/ directory that uses the library only through its public API.
A code example in a documentation comment that cargo test compiles and runs.
A /// comment that documents the next item in Markdown and is turned into HTML by cargo doc.
